subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 4: Vocabulary and Grammar – Money and have to / don’t have to
outcomes: Say eight money words like purse, wallet, save and spend.
Use have to / don't have to for things that are necessary or not.
Ask and answer Do you have to …? questions.

tf.s: "Don't have to" means you must not do it.
tf.why: don't have to = it is not necessary.

tf.s: We say "He have to get some pocket money."
tf.why: With he/she we use has to: He has to get some pocket money.

tf.s: A money box is a place to keep money at home.
tf.why: You can save coins in a money box.

tf.s: When you save money, you use it to buy sweets.
tf.why: When you save money, you keep it. When you spend it, you use it.

tf.s: A purse is a small bag for money that women often carry.
"Does Dana have to buy some shoes?" is a correct question.
A short answer to "Do you have to study?" is "Yes, I have."
tf.why: The short answer is: Yes, I do.

tf.s: "She's got all the ingredients, so she doesn't have to go to the greengrocer's." is correct.
tf.why: She has everything, so it is not necessary to go.

boxes.q: Where do you keep money at home?
o: in a purse at the shop
boxes.why: A money box keeps money safe at home.

boxes.q: Complete: He ______ get some pocket money.
boxes.why: With he we use has to.
Save = keep money; spend = use it.

boxes.q: Make a question: you / have to / buy that boat?
o: Do you have to buy that boat?
You do have to buy that boat?
Have you to buy that boat?

boxes.q: I've got a lot of pocket money, so I ______ save any money.
boxes.why: It is not necessary to save.

boxes.q: We have a difficult exam tomorrow, so we ______ study a lot this evening.
boxes.why: Studying is necessary before an exam.

boxes.q: Complete: Shops ______ things and people buy them.
Does Nawaf have to buy some shoes? (yes)
Which sentence is about something NOT necessary?
o: We don't have to buy toys.

boxes.q: Money that parents give children every week is ______.

hunt.q: Keep coins at home in it

mcq.q: What is the difference between "I have to" and "I don't have to"?
o: have to = necessary; don't have to = not necessary
have to = past; don't have to = future
have to = question; don't have to = answer
mcq.why: have to shows something is necessary.

mcq.q: Which group has only money words?

o: a small flat case for money
mcq.why: People keep money and cards in a wallet.

mcq.q: Which word do we use with he and she?
mcq.why: He has to, she has to.

mcq.q: Ask about Dana: buy some shoes?
o: Does Dana have to buy some shoes?
Do Dana has to buy some shoes?
Dana does have to buys some shoes?
Has Dana to buy some shoes?
mcq.why: Does + Dana + have to + base verb?

mcq.q: Your family needs food every week. Which sentence is correct?
o: We have to buy food every week.
We don't have to buy food every week.
We has to buy food every week.
We have to buys food every week.
mcq.why: Food is necessary, so we use have to.

mcq.q: You have no homework tonight. What do you say?
o: I don't have to do homework tonight.
I have to do homework tonight.
I doesn't have to do homework tonight.
I has to do homework tonight.
mcq.why: It is not necessary, so don't have to.

mcq.q: Ali puts his pocket money in his money box every week. Is he saving or spending?
mcq.why: He keeps his money, so he is saving.

o: He have to get some pocket money.
We don't have to buy toys.
mcq.why: With he we say has to.

mcq.q: Sara buys sweets every day with her pocket money. What is true?
mcq.why: Using money to buy things is spending.
